summary.headline: GRSE posted record FY26: revenue INR 7,002 crore (+38%) and PAT INR 748 crore (+42%), with order book down to INR 15,324 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported best-ever Q4 and FY26 results, with Q4 revenue of INR 2,119 crore (+29% YoY) and PAT of INR 303 crore (from INR 244 crore). Eight warships were delivered in FY26, including three on a single day, and the company said revenue from the bridges vertical crossed INR 200 crore for the first time. The order book fell to INR 15,324 crore, the first time it has dropped below INR 20,000 crore in five years, which management attributed to faster execution. The NGC corvette contract (~INR 33,000 crore, GRSE as L1) is still unsigned; management now expects signing in the June quarter, and it pushes NGC revenue recognition to H2 FY28.

lower; first time below INR 20,000 crore in five years

segments.name: Warship / defence shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Warship order book about INR 11,361 crore. P-17 Alpha has about INR 5,868 crore remaining, NGOPV INR 5,168 crore and ASW Shallow Water Craft INR 2,035 crore. Eight warships delivered in FY26.

segments.name: Non-defence / commercial vessels
segments.commentary: Order book about INR 3,369 crore across Ocean Research Vessel (INR 749 crore), Coastal Research Vessels (INR 260 crore), Acoustic Research Ship (INR 456 crore), hybrid ferries (INR 207 crore), Multipurpose Vessels (INR 1,345 crore) and dredger (INR 66 crore).

segments.name: Naval guns and portable steel bridges
segments.commentary: Seven naval surface guns delivered in FY26, four completed Sea Acceptance Trials. 110 portable steel bridges delivered, including 30 for export; bridges revenue above INR 200 crore for the first time, export revenue above INR 270 crore.

guidance_outlook: NGC contract (~INR 33,000 crore) expected to be signed in the June 2026 quarter; no revenue planned in FY27 or H1 FY28; revenue to start in H2 FY28, major chunk from FY29.

FY27 revenue accrual expected to be 'very healthy', in line with the last three to four years; FY28 to be padded by remaining projects, NGOPV, commercial vessels and new orders. Management declined to confirm FY28 revenue will not dip.
EBITDA margins expected to be similar in FY27, and management will try to maintain similar margins in FY28 and FY29.
Capacity to rise from 28 platforms to 32 ships by end of calendar 2026 via modernisation; plans for two brownfield and two greenfield yards (West Bengal and Gujarat).

Pipeline of about INR 1,50,000 crore of AoN-accorded RFPs (excluding NGC), with P-17 Bravo (~INR 70,000 crore) RFP expected in the current quarter; MCV (~INR 32,000 crore) and LPD (~INR 35,000 crore) RFPs by end of FY27.
capex_capacity: Current shipbuilding capacity is 28 platforms; expected to rise to 32 ships by end of calendar 2026 through in-premises modernisation.
Planned expansion: two brownfield shipbuilding facilities in West Bengal and two greenfield facilities (one in West Bengal, one in Gujarat).
ASW Shallow Water Craft: four delivered, two at ~80% construction with basin trials done (delivery by mid-calendar 2026), last two at ~60% (delivery in FY27).
P-17 Alpha last ship at ~74% physical progress, delivery targeted in calendar 2026. NGOPV first ship launch planned on 20 May 2026; project completion in FY29.

Ocean Research Vessel ~50% complete, launch planned in calendar 2026. Acoustic Research Ship ~20% complete. 13 hybrid ferries (6 x 200-PAX, 7 x 100-PAX) to finish by end FY27; first two 100-PAX launches planned in May 2026. German 12-ship MPV: keel laid on three ships. Bangladesh dredger launch planned in FY27.
demand_pricing: Next Generation Corvette (NGC): price negotiations complete, ~INR 33,000 crore, GRSE is L1; contract slipped from 31 March 2026 target, now expected in June quarter; management says no red flags. Electronics is 55-60% of equipment cost, with BEL as a major sister-PSU supplier.

Live tenders: Multipurpose Vessels (2 ships, ~INR 1,500 crore, bid submitted), OPV for Coast Guard (5 ships, ~INR 2,000 crore) and 22 Interceptor Boats (~INR 1,000 crore), bids due around end May or early June 2026.

Upcoming RFPs in ~3 months: 120 Fast Interceptor Craft (~INR 3,500 crore, split 80/40), 31 Follow-On Water Jet FACs (~INR 3,500 crore) and seven P-17 Bravo (~INR 70,000 crore, split 4/3). MCV (12 ships, ~INR 32,000 crore, 8/4) and LPD (4 ships, ~INR 35,000 crore, 2/2) RFPs expected by end FY27.

Commercial tenders from Ministry of Shipping: four Platform Support Vessels (INR 1,200-1,500 crore), four MR tankers, six VLGCs and six Aframax vessels. European ship owners are in dialogue, citing pricing and quality versus China and Korea.
Cost escalation: existing contracts are fixed price, and vendor orders were placed earlier, so management reports no material impact; new bids will factor in commodity risk.

qa_highlights.question: Statutory defence committee report shows contracts expected over two years for warships and survey vessels fell to ~INR 18,900 crore from ~INR 42,000 crore. What does this mean for government focus?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said the INR 18,900 crore figure reflects annual fund outflow, not intent. He cited AoNs, RFPs and approved Navy and Coast Guard roadmaps as evidence of continued focus.

qa_highlights.question: Relevance of conventional platforms versus autonomous vessels, and GRSE's strategy in autonomy.
qa_highlights.answer: Conventional platforms remain relevant for armament and endurance. GRSE has developed subsurface and surface autonomous vessels, supplied one to a DRDO organisation, and targets the XL AUV under Make projects in 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the revenue in the 31 March provisional figure materially different from the final reported number?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had kept a conservative provisional figure because three ships were delivered on the last day. After formalising deliveries and revenue with the Navy, final revenue came to about INR 7,200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NGC delayed, and when will it be signed? Will there be one or two winners on smaller projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Price negotiations are complete. Contract signing was expected by 31 March but is now expected in the June quarter, with no red flags. Smaller projects are mostly single-yard awards, with 120 FAC and P-17 Bravo split between two yards.

qa_highlights.question: When will NGC revenue start and how will revenue and EBITDA margins look for FY27-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: NGC revenue recognition starts in H2 FY28, with the major chunk from FY29. Margins are expected to be similar in FY27 and the company will try to maintain them in FY28-FY29. Management did not confirm no FY28 revenue dip.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY25 and FY26 margins inflated by provision write-backs, and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Analyst cited 8.3% EBITDA margin in FY25 and 11.6% in FY26. Management said the current year margins will be similar but would not give a specific percentage, saying it is only Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NGC vendor ecosystem and electronics content?
qa_highlights.answer: Equipment and systems are ~65% of project cost; electronics is 55-60% of that and machinery and systems 40-45%. First downstream orders expected within three months of contract signing, majority within three to six months. BEL expected to be a key partner.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company take large European commercial orders and target higher margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commercial export projects will be selected for good margins. Warship projects, at ~INR 675 crore per ASW ship, still carry the best money and margins. Hybrid large vessels are being targeted.

qa_highlights.question: How are commodity cost increases handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing contracts are fixed price and vendor contracts are fixed price too, so no material impact was reported. Time delays on steel and industrial gas were marginal. New bids will factor in uncertainty.

risks_watch: NGC contract signing has already slipped from 31 March to June quarter; any further delay would push the revenue ramp and reduce FY28 visibility.
Order book of INR 15,324 crore is down sharply; FY28 revenue is not guaranteed without new order wins, and no revenue recognition from NGC is planned until H2 FY28.
Margin sustainability: FY26 margin included provision write-backs per analyst. Management has not quantified the sustainable margin level.
Commodity and steel cost escalation on new bids and possible time delays; existing contracts are fixed price.

Unresolved question on the variable depth sonar for ASW ships (buyer-furnished, still in development). Management said there is no financial impact on the PBG. Management declined to comment on the NGOPV and NGC sonar profile.
Timing of RFPs for P-17 Bravo, MCV and LPD, and the expansion capex execution (brownfield and greenfield yards).

summary.management_tone: Confident on execution, shipbuilding pipeline and the June-quarter NGC signing, with "no red flags". Cautious and evasive on specifics: declined to give a sustainable EBITDA margin percentage ("we are only in the 1st Quarter"), would not confirm FY28 revenue will not dip, and withheld NGOPV/NGC sonar details as confidential.
